question: Polar bears and penguins have NEVER met in the wild. True or false?

post.premise: Polar bears and penguins live at opposite ends of the planet
post.bait: Every picture of them together was staged or drawn.
post.sources_line: IUCN Red List; WWF; Galápagos Conservancy; Britannica

youtube.title: Do polar bears eat penguins? True or false: they have NEVER met in the wild 🐧
youtube.description:
Every Christmas advert puts them on the same ice. The map says something else.
One of these animals lives only in the far north, the other only south of the equator — or right on it. Guess before the line draws across the globe.
Subscribe for a wildlife quiz you can argue about every day.

research.topic: Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) live only in the Arctic; penguins live only in the Southern Hemisphere (Galápagos penguin reaches the equator); the two have never met in the wild

myths.reality: They never meet: polar bears are Arctic-only, penguins Southern-Hemisphere-only (the Galápagos penguin reaches the equator). Images of them together are composites or drawings.

landscape.our_gap: Animal-fact Shorts state the myth over stock footage; nobody draws the equator across a real map, pins the bears above it and the penguins below it, then flies to the Galápagos and to Alaska.

iucn_polar.title: Ursus maritimus (Polar Bear)
iucn_polar.notes: circumpolar Arctic distribution: Canada, Greenland, Norway (Svalbard), Russia, United States (Alaska); no Southern Hemisphere range

britannica_polar.title: polar bear
britannica_polar.notes: found throughout the Arctic region; Churchill, Manitoba; Svalbard; Alaska's North Slope

iucn_galapagos.title: Spheniscus mendiculus (Galápagos Penguin)
iucn_galapagos.notes: endemic to the Galápagos Islands, Ecuador; the only penguin whose range reaches the equator (northern tip of Isabela just north of 0°)

wwf_penguins.title: Penguins — where do penguins live?
wwf_penguins.notes: all 18 species live in the Southern Hemisphere, from Antarctica to South Africa (Boulders Beach), Australia (Phillip Island little penguins) and the Galápagos

britannica_penguin.title: penguin
britannica_penguin.notes: penguins are confined to the Southern Hemisphere; the Galápagos penguin lives at the equator; none occur in the Arctic

wiki_penguin.title: Penguin
wiki_penguin.notes: live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere; only the Galápagos penguin is found north of the equator (barely); no wild penguins in the Arctic

wiki_polar.title: Polar bear
wiki_polar.notes: range: Arctic Ocean and surrounding land in five nations; Alaska populations (Chukchi, Southern Beaufort); Churchill 'polar bear capital'
